title: Homeownership Regimes and Low Fertility
source_note: Housing Studies. Comparative homeownership-regime typology (access to ownership x mortgage market development) against low fertility. Named in the HYPOTHESES-v5 seminal field; VERIFIED. Typology/framework rather than an identified effect estimate, so it seeds the theory stream and does not count toward empirical recall.

title: House prices and birth rates: The impact of the real estate market on the decision to have a baby
source_note: Journal of Public Economics (OpenAlex dates the record 2013 online, issue 2014; v5 says 2014). THE tenure-split anchor: US MSA price variation, effects of opposite sign for owners and non-owners. NBER digest summary reports roughly -1% births for non-owners and +4.5% for owners per 10% price rise -- NOT verified at source; confirm at extraction. Preprint twins: NBER w17485 (10.3386/w17485).

title: Do Family Wealth Shocks Affect Fertility Choices? Evidence from the Housing Market
source_note: Review of Economics and Statistics (OpenAlex dates 2012, Crossref 2013). WALL 1 TEST CASE: listed as seminal for BOTH C.2.c and C.3.e in HYPOTHESES-v5. Under the 2026-07-31 ruling its identifying variation is a housing price shock, so it is C.2.c's; C.3.e should cross-ref. Preprint twin: SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.1544607.
container: The Review of Economics and Statistics

title: Home prices, fertility, and early-life health outcomes
source_note: Journal of Public Economics. Denmark. v5 lists this as 'Daysal Lovenheim and Wasser 2021' -- author list is incomplete in v5 (omits Siersbaek); title VERIFIED. Carries a second, non-fertility outcome stream (birth weight, prematurity) which is OFF_OUTCOME for this chapter. Preprint twins: NBER w27469, SSRN 3636646, SSRN 3644070.

title: Do surging house prices discourage fertility? Global evidence, 1870-2012
source_note: Labour Economics. PHENOMENA-SCOPE CHALLENGE: the panel runs 1870-2012 and the abstract frames the result against the fertility transition, i.e. squarely into FDT territory, while HYPOTHESES-v5 scopes C.2.c to SDT only. Reported effect -0.01 to -0.03 births per woman per 10% real house price rise (from a secondary summary, NOT verified at source). Preprint twin: SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.4424655.

title: Housing and fertility: a macro-level, multi-country investigation, 1993-2017
source_note: Housing Studies. Multi-country macro panel; the closest thing found to a synthesis of the cross-national evidence, though it is a primary study and not a systematic review.

title: House price, fertility rates and reproductive intentions
source_note: China Economic Review. Carries both a realized-fertility and a stated-intention outcome, so it will need the OUTCOME_LEVEL tag and cannot pool the two together.

title: The Effect of House Price on Fertility: Evidence from Hong Kong
source_note: Economic Inquiry. Hong Kong -- an extreme-price, low-ownership setting, useful for the OWNERSHIP_RATE moderator and for the space-constraint reading.

title: Housing wealth, fertility intentions and fertility
source_note: Journal of Housing Economics. Australia (HILDA). Carries both intentions and realized fertility -- OUTCOME_LEVEL tag required.

title: Housing wealth, fertility and children's health in China: A regression discontinuity design
source_note: Journal of Health Economics. RD design -- likely one of the stronger identification strategies in the pool; flag for the risk-of-bias exclusion-restriction domain.

title: Low Fertility and the Housing Market: Evidence from Swedish Regional Data
source_note: European Journal of Population. Swedish regional panel. Same author as the SJPE reverse-direction paper below -- the pair is useful for testing that the screen separates direction.

title: Interrelationships Between Childbearing and Housing Transitions in the Family Life Course
source_note: Demography. Jointly models housing and childbearing transitions -- the canonical statement of the anticipatory-sorting threat (people move in anticipation of births). Value is as the identification-threat anchor, not as an effect estimate.

title: Fertility differences by housing type
source_note: Demographic Research. Housing type/size rather than price -- the 'space constraints' half of the hypothesis title, which the 2026-07-31 ruling demotes out of the primary price pools. Heavy residential-selection threat.

title: Housing context and childbearing in Sweden: a cohort study
source_note: Housing Studies. Housing context/conditions rather than price.

title: Do House Prices Affect Fertility Behavior in China? An Empirical Examination
source_note: International Regional Science Review.

title: The effect of house prices on fertility: evidence from Canada
source_note: Economics (E-Journal). Open access.

title: The Crowding-out Effect of Homeownership on Fertility
source_note: Journal of Family and Economic Issues. Tenure as treatment rather than price -- borderline against the 2026-07-31 ruling; a useful boundary case for the RA gate.
container: Journal of Family and Economic Issues

title: Housing as a Fertility Trap: The Inability of States, Markets, or Families to Provide Adequate Housing in East Central Europe
source_note: East European Politics and Societies. Institutional/comparative; East Central Europe. Likely closer to theory than to an identified estimate.

title: Homeownership and fertility intentions among migrant population in urban China
source_note: Housing Studies. Stated-intention outcome; tenure as treatment.

title: Impacts of Housing Booms on Fertility in China: A Perspective From Homeownership
source_note: International Regional Science Review. Explicitly frames the tenure split -- a candidate for the tenure-split stratum.

title: A day late and a dollar short: Liquidity and household formation among student borrowers
source_note: DECOY. Journal of Financial Economics. Identifying variation is liquidity/student debt, not housing prices -- routes to C.3.e/C.3.g under the 2026-07-31 ruling despite surfacing on a homeownership+fertility query. Tests Wall 1 in the credit direction.

title: Rising housing prices and marriage delays in China: Evidence from the urban land transaction policy
source_note: DECOY. Cities. Housing price variation (in scope) but the outcome is marriage delay, not fertility -- mechanism/context, cross-ref A.7. Tests whether the screen enforces the fertility-outcome requirement.

title: Demographic changes and the housing market
source_note: DECOY. Regional Science and Urban Economics. Runs demography -> housing market, the reverse of the chapter's direction.

title: Fertility Cycles, Age Structure and Housing Demand
source_note: DECOY. Scottish Journal of Political Economy. Fertility -> housing demand. Same author as the forward-direction EJP paper above, which makes the pair a direct test that the screen routes on direction rather than on author or topic.

title: The impact of housing prices on residents' health: a systematic review
source_note: CHANNEL-1 NEAR MISS, recorded for the audit trail. BMC Public Health; SCOPUS+PubMed to June 2022; 23 studies across mental (7), physical (9), and combined (7) health. It is the only systematic review found anywhere near this hypothesis, and its outcome is health, not fertility. Its sole fertility-literature overlap is Daysal et al. 2021, included for that paper's birth-weight and prematurity outcomes rather than its fertility estimate. Contributes ZERO new empirical fertility anchors.
